body: [A10] Scope addition from the #234 baseline (PR #638, ranking lever 2): the SRP timer-arm FIFOs at `KL_srp_top.sv:947` (2,304 FF + a 648-LUT read mux at 1x1) join this issue, measured and reduced with the per-stream evaluation (lever 4). Ruling: https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/234 (manager rulings on PR #638).

[A10] **Lane for #230:** the second area lever of epic #229. Executor: [A523], in the processor repository on branch `pp230-srp-area` from processor `main` `c4cb84ff`. Reviewers: [R458] (internal) and [R459] (external).

**Levers in scope** (from the #234 baseline, PR #638):
- **Lever 2: the SRP timer-arm FIFOs** (`KL_srp_top.sv:947`): 2,304 FF and a 648-LUT read mux at 1x1. Estimated saving: about 2,300 FF and 580 LUT.
- **Lever 4: SRP per-stream evaluation:** about 440 LUT at 1x1 and about 3,100 at 8x8 (212 and 227 LUT per context).
- **#230's own scope:**
  - measure the talker FSM, listener FSM, top glue, decoder, encoder and admission separately;
  - find logic replicated per stream;
  - share or time-multiplex it where protocol latency permits;
  - pack per-stream state into RAM-friendly structures;
  - make inactive slots vanish at elaboration in smaller shapes;
  - document the marginal cost per talker and per listener.

**Rules:**
- **Behaviour is identical.** No port, parameter-meaning or register change, and no protocol-visible timing change: SRP (IEEE 802.1Q-2018 clause 35) declaration and timer behaviour as today. If a lever needs any of these, STOP with the trade-off, as lane #232 did.
- **Prove the equivalence.** Every processor suite, every SRP campaign and the `tb/pp_top` campaigns pass at the same counts, plus a lockstep bench of the old against the new `KL_srp_top` (as #232 did for the notify block) with planted controls.
- **The 100 MHz criterion** is judged at the declared 50 MHz (#565), as ruled for #234 and #232.

**Measurement:** #638's recipe and gate (milan-fpga `234-area-baseline` at `68d26ea0`), in a scratch parent that is never pushed.
- **Base:** dev `5fabb46e` + processor `c4cb84ff` + `parent-adoption-c8-bbf704ec.patch` + `parent-adoption-p2-p1-1269cdaf.patch`.
- **Head:** the same, with this lane's processor.
- **Runs:** out-of-context 1x1 and 8x8, and the integrated route, with per-sub-block figures for `u_srp`. Vivado one instance at a time, each under `flock /tmp/milan-vivado.lock`.

**Parent:** the consumer set of 17 at dev `5fabb46e` with both patches. Gate 16's T30 checks are recorded against #643 if they fail.

**Output:** HANDOFF.md and PR-BODY.md (processor PR; "Relates to milan-fpga#230" and "#229", or "Closes milan-fpga#230" only if every item is met). Then REVIEW READY with the head on this issue. Do not push.

Do not edit or delete any existing comment.

[A523] STOP
Head: `65324390d1b83c4587f299d06597f7a571d7fa61` on local branch `pp230-srp-area` (processor), two one-line commits on `main` `c4cb84ff`; not pushed, as assigned.

**STOP on lever 4's shared evaluator only.** Sharing the per-stream evaluation across contexts needs a protocol-visible timing change and a decoder port change. Everything else in the assignment is done and validated at this head. There is no port, parameter, register or behaviour change and no parent patch.

**Lever 2, done, cycle-exact.** The SRP timer-arm FIFOs were one two-dimensional array written for both FIFOs in one process (`KL_srp_top.sv:947` on `main`): 2,304 flops at 1x1.
- **The change.** Each FIFO is now its own memory (`tf_tk_ram_r`, `tf_ls_ram_r`), with one write and one registered read port, and is `RAM32M x 8`. Pointers, depth, full guard and heads are unchanged.
- **The attribute.** `ram_style = "distributed"` is needed: without it the registered read cost a RAMB36 per FIFO.
- **Measured** (standalone 1x1, SRP top glue): 907 -> 354 LUT, 2,836 -> 545 FF. #638 estimated about 580 LUT and 2,300 FF.

**Lever 4, storage part done, cycle-exact.**
- **What moved.** What only the walks and the admission walk read is now distributed RAM: the talker's walk-only TSpec/priority/rank/latency fields, the admission slopes, and the walks' copies of {stream_id, DA, VLAN} from three contexts up. At one or two contexts a 2-way multiplexer is cheaper than a second copy, so the walks read the matcher's flops there (measured at 2 and 9 contexts).
- **Measured.** Talker, listener and admission together: 1x1 -37 LUT and -168 FF; 8x8 -791 LUT and -762 FF.

**Vivado** (#638 recipe and gate at `68d26ea0`; base dev `5fabb46e` + processor `c4cb84ff` + c8-bbf704ec + p2-p1-1269cdaf; head the same with this processor; 50 MHz):

| Endpoint | LUT | FF | Slice | RAMB36/18 | DSP | WNS / WHS ns | `u_srp` LUT (LUTRAM) / FF |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Route base | 51,434 | 59,691 | 15,847 | 79/27 | 14 | +0.079 / +0.014 | 4,340 (180) / 6,263 |
| Route head | 51,005 | 57,262 | 15,837 | 79/27 | 14 | +0.354 / +0.036 | 3,711 (298) / 3,839 |
| 1x1 base / head | 24,930 / 24,258 | 25,465 / 23,130 | - | 21/3 | 8 | estimate -2.059 / -1.874 | 4,558 / 3,988; 6,438 / 3,979 |
| 8x8 base / head | 32,584 / 31,109 | 34,211 / 30,648 | - | 26/5 | 8 | estimate -2.161 / -1.495 | 8,705 / 7,313; 11,192 / 7,747 |

- **Routes.** Both are complete (0 routing errors), and both meet BUILDING §5 at 50 MHz. The head route took 33 minutes against base's 83.
- **#638's gate.** Head: rc 0 on all three endpoints ("re-baseline recommended"). Base: rc 1 on all three, the un-rebaselined next adoption (`u_d3` growth since `631eeb34`), as on #232.

**The rest of #230's scope.**
- **Blocks measured separately.** Talker FSM, listener FSM, top glue, decoder, encoder, admission, domain and VLAN, at the route, 1x1 and 8x8, base and head: HANDOFF section 5.3.
- **Storage inventory.** Each SRP structure with its intended and actual primitive and the Vivado report lines: HANDOFF section 3 and processor 10 §5.1. No SRP buffer spills into flops at head; SRP's only block RAM is still the decoder's RAMB18.
- **Inactive slots.** The 1x1 configuration has none. Per-stream structures are sized by `N_STREAM_OUT_P`/`N_STREAM_IN_P` = 2 at 1x1 (the stream and CRF), and the census shows exactly two contexts.
- **Marginal cost** (standalone, (8x8 - 1x1) / 7). One more talker costs about 200 LUT and 240 FF (base 286/322); one more listener about 210 LUT and 280 FF (base 227/278). The whole SRP engine goes from 592 to 475 LUT and from 679 to 538 FF per source-and-sink pair. This is recorded in 10 §5.1; #229 is not updated from this lane.

**Validation, all rc 0, no pipes, except gate 16 below.**
- **Lockstep.** `main`'s `KL_srp_top` beside the head's, with the same inputs every cycle, comparing all 51 outputs and 56 internal signals:
  - 48 runs x 1,000,000 cycles over 2/2, 9/9, 1/1, 3/5, 8/8, and 2/2 at the default cadences, with 647 mid-run resets and unreset memories randomised differently in each model;
  - 0 mismatches.
  - Sixteen planted controls were each caught.
- **Processor suites.** `lint_hdl.sh` 41/41, plus the changed modules at 1, 2, 3 and 9 contexts. `run_suites.sh`: 1,021,423 checks at base and head, every suite equal. `make check`, `gen_matrix --check` and `syn/yosys/run.sh` (36/36) pass.
- **Campaigns, base and head.** Every arm's record is identical:
  - srp_top 90/90 (all 73 patches apply) and srp_admission 12/12;
  - maap 32 and adp 32;
  - pp_top ctr 18, notify 40/40, acmp 19/19, aecp 60, dispatch 41, d3 110/110, gsi 20, name_wr 1.
- **Parent consumer set.** At dev `5fabb46e` + both patches with this processor, 16 of 17 rc 0. Gate 16 exits 2 on exactly its two T30 INTERNAL law checks, with #643's P1 figures (227/292, 285/292, delay 8.830..9.034 ticks). Base `c4cb84ff` gives the same two failures with the same figures, so they are recorded against #643. The builder gate gives "all pass except gate 11 not run (mf48 tree)" with the host's Make 4.4.1, as in P1's record.

**Lever 4's shared evaluator: the ruling asked.** #638 estimated "one evaluator per FSM" at about 440 LUT at 1x1 and 3,100 at 8x8. What is per stream now is evaluated for every context in one cycle by contract:
- **The matcher.** `KL_srp_decoder` emits one value per cycle with no ready, and every context compares it in that cycle.
- **The transitions.** `periodic!`, LeaveAll and a matched value reach every context in that cycle.
- **The published levels.** They are per-stream ports.

The options:
- (a) One evaluator per FSM, with contexts in RAM evaluated one per cycle. The decoder gains a ready (a port change). Registration indications and LISTENER_REG_CHANGE move by up to M - 1 or N - 1 cycles. A timing change.
- (b) Keep the parallel evaluation (landed): cycle-exact.

Requested: (b) as final for #230, or (a) as an input to the redesign (#640). With (b), this head is ready for review as it stands.

**Packet.** HANDOFF.md (changes with file:line, the storage inventory with the Vivado report lines, tests with their controls, the before/after figures and receipts, the suite, campaign and parent tables) and PR-BODY.md for the processor PR ("Relates to milan-fpga#230", "Relates to milan-fpga#229"; no closing keyword, since lever 4 needs this ruling and #230's "documented in #229" item is outside this lane's posting rights). Raw reports and logs stay in scratch, with their digests in HANDOFF.

[A10] **Ruling on [A523] STOP (5977826098): (b).** The parallel per-stream evaluation stays as landed and is final for #230: the area track before the next adoption is cycle-exact by charter, and (a) moves registration indications and LISTENER_REG_CHANGE by up to M - 1 / N - 1 cycles and adds a decoder ready port. (a), one evaluator per FSM with contexts in RAM (#638 estimate ~440 LUT at 1x1, ~3,100 at 8x8), is recorded as an input to the redesign in #640. Head `65324390` goes to review as it stands; the processor PR opens now and #230 closes manually at the processor merge.
